description: Verifies the traversable wormhole and the warp bubble: the Morris-Thorne metric at the throat, a radial photon crossing the throat with the adaptive integrator, the shaping function limits of the Alcubierre bubble and the geometric invariants of both metrics.

checks.label: the time component equals -1 for a vanishing redshift potential
the proper radial component equals 1
the polar component equals the squared throat radius
the azimuthal component equals the squared throat radius at the equator
every adaptive step of the throat transit succeeds
the photon passes from the negative to the positive side of the wormhole
the photon passes within 0.2 of the throat
the photon emerges on the far side up to l = 10
Morris-Thorne: the inverse metric times the metric reproduces the identity
Morris-Thorne: the metric tensor is symmetric relative to its largest component
Morris-Thorne: the metric determinant is negative, which gives a Lorentzian signature
Morris-Thorne: the analytic connection is symmetric in its lower indices
Morris-Thorne: the analytic connection matches eighth-order finite differences relative to the largest symbol of its row
the shaping function equals 1 at the bubble centre
the shaping function vanishes far from the bubble
the inverse metric reproduces the identity at the centre
Alcubierre: the inverse metric times the metric reproduces the identity
Alcubierre: the metric tensor is symmetric relative to its largest component
Alcubierre: the metric determinant is negative, which gives a Lorentzian signature
Alcubierre: the analytic connection is symmetric in its lower indices
Alcubierre: the analytic connection matches eighth-order finite differences relative to the largest symbol of its row
